findings.description: Candidate consumes the records iterable twice. For one-shot iterators, the second iteration yields nothing, producing an empty dictionary. This violates the contract that the function must return a mapping for all names.
findings.evidence: The function calls sum(...) over records, which exhausts the iterator. It then iterates over records again in the comprehension. If records is an iterator (e.g., a generator), the second loop sees no items, returning an empty dict. Example: candidate.allocate((("a",1), ("b",2)), 100) returns {} instead of the expected mapping. This behavior violates the requirement that the function must handle any iterable, including one-shot iterators, and return a mapping for every name.

review.summary: The implementation incorrectly consumes the records iterator twice, breaking the contract for one-shot iterators.
